author: Antonialock
body:
Hi, this isn't really an annotation issue but I was looking at 
PTHR42862 DELTA-1-PYRROLINE-5-CARBOXYLATE DEHYDROGENASE 1
(EC=1.2.1.88) and I wonder if it would make sense to rename this panther family 1-PYRROLINE-5-CARBOXYLATE DEHYDROGENASE
(I think it is written Delta^1-pyrroline.....not delta-1-pyrroline....)
title: PAINT issue: PTHR42862

author: marcfeuermann
body:
I've checked the name. It seems fine here. Just to be sure, your request is about replacing the ^ sign, not removing the DELTA ?
Marc.

author: Antonialock
body: I was just wondering if "DELTA-1-PYRROLINE" made sense, spelt like that, I wasn't sure if it looked odd.

author: marcfeuermann
body:
Ah okay, sorry, my neurons are a little bit tired today. In fact, depending on the source, several names are used. 
From wikipedia: Other names in common use include **delta-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate dehydrogenase, 1-pyrroline dehydrogenase, pyrroline-5-carboxylate dehydrogenase, pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid dehydrogenase, L-pyrroline-5-carboxylate-NAD+ oxidoreductase, and 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate:NAD+ oxidoreductase.** 
In UniProt they seem to use mostly **delta-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate dehydrogenase** 
https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P30038/entry
That's why I would favor not to modify the name. But I can change it if you think the shorter one is more appropriate.
Cheers,
Marc.
